Use this page the first time you log in to the research server at Statistics
Denmark (DST), and come back to it for the log-off routine. It takes you from the
browser login to an RStudio project in your own folder. It assumes you already
have access: a personal ident, a project number, and the FortiToken app that
gives you the one-time code. When you are done you can run R code on the server
and you know the rules that apply while you do.

DST's own connection guides (PDF, in Danish, with screenshots) for Windows, Mac
and Linux are listed on [DST's page about the research
machines](https://www.dst.dk/da/TilSalg/data-til-forskning/analyseplatform/forskermaskinen).
The steps below follow them.

## Connect to the server

### Step 1 - Install Windows App (Mac only)

On a Mac, open the App Store, search for "Windows App" (from Microsoft) and
install it.

On Windows you install nothing: the login page downloads an `.rdp` file, and you
open it.

### Step 2 - Log in

1. Go to [remote.dst.dk](https://remote.dst.dk) in your browser.
2. Enter your ident (4 letters) as username and your code for remote.dst.dk as
   password.
3. Enter the 6-digit token code shown in the FortiToken Mobile app on your phone.
4. Click the server you want to connect to. You see only the buttons you have
   access to. For R, choose **Python/R**. If you choose **FSE Windows** instead,
   you land on a selection desktop and click through to Python/R from there.
5. Log in to the server with your project ident, which is your ident followed by
   the project number: `dstfse\abcd123456` (or `abcd123456@dstfse.local`), and
   the password for that project user. Do not tick "remember my credentials":
   DST's guide warns that it gives problems when you change password.

### If you cannot log in {#login-fails}

DST's page about the [research
machines](https://www.dst.dk/da/TilSalg/data-til-forskning/analyseplatform/forskermaskinen)
has separate guides (PDF, in Danish) for changing your password, resetting a
forgotten one, installing and setting up FortiToken, and connecting from abroad.
If none of them covers your problem, contact DST's service desk; the email,
phone number and opening hours are in the footer of the connection guides.

### Step 3 - Find or create your own folder

Open File Explorer and navigate to the `workspaces` folder under your project.
Create a folder with your name or ident if it does not already exist:

```
E:/workdata/[projectnumber]/workspaces/[your-name]/
```

Recommended structure within your folder:

```
[your-name]/
  [your-project-name]/
    R/              ← all your scripts (.R files)
    datasets/       ← intermediate results (.rds files, local to DST only)
    output/         ← tables and figures ready for repatriation
```

### Step 4 - Mac keyboard: switch to Unicode mode at every connection {#mac-keyboard}

On a Mac, special characters such as `` ` ``, `$`, `\`, `@`, `{` and `}` do not
come out right in the remote session by default. Switch the keyboard to Unicode
mode with Ctrl + Cmd + U inside the remote window (or in the menu bar:
Connections, then Keyboard Mode).

  | Character | Mac shortcut in Unicode mode |
  | --------- | ---------------------------- |
  | Pipe `\|` | Option + i                   |
  | `[`       | Option + 8                   |
  | `]`       | Option + 9                   |
  | `{`       | Option + Shift + 8           |
  | `}`       | Option + Shift + 9           |
  | `\`       | Option + Shift + 7           |

In RStudio on the server, code is run with Ctrl+Enter (not Cmd+Enter).

## Create your R project

An R project collects all your scripts, output files and settings in one folder.
Give each study its own project.

A project is first of all a folder: you still save your own files in it (in
`R/`, `datasets/`, `output/`). What it adds is the `.Rproj` file. When you open
the project, RStudio sets the **working directory** to the folder where `.Rproj`
lives. So `getwd()` points to your project folder, and you can use relative
paths (`datasets/cohort.rds`) instead of writing the full path or
`setwd("E:/...")` at the top of every script. Each project also keeps its own
settings and history, so studies do not get mixed up.

1. Open RStudio
2. **File → New Project → New Directory → New Project**
3. Give the project a name and choose a location under your workspace folder
4. Click **Create Project**

Run `getwd()` now and you get the path to your project, e.g.
`E:/workdata/[projectnumber]/workspaces/[your-name]/[your-project-name]`

Two settings to change once, under **Tools → Global Options**:

- **Do not save the workspace:** under General, set "Save workspace to .RData
  on exit" to Never. Otherwise RStudio asks "Save workspace image?" every time
  you close it; the answer is always No.
- **Optional, for a faster start:** under Packages, uncheck "Enable packages
  pane". You use `library()` and `install.packages()` in the code anyway.

::: {#update-duckplyr .callout-important}
**Reinstall `duckplyr` at the start of every session**

DST has `duckplyr` pre-installed, but in an old version that is missing
functionality, so several patterns in this guide will not work with it. Install
the current version from CRAN, and repeat after every log-out or server reset:
the reset puts the old pre-installed version back. `duckplyr` is the package
behind `read_parquet_duckdb()` and, from fastreg 0.14.3, behind
`read_register()`.

```r
install.packages(c("duckplyr", "duckdb")) # current CRAN versions - run before library()
packageVersion("duckplyr") # check the version in this session; 1.1 or newer is fine
```
:::

## The rules you sign up to, in short

You certify to these before you get access, and breaking them carries
[sanctions (page in
Danish)](https://www.dst.dk/da/TilSalg/data-til-forskning/regler-og-datasikkerhed/sanktionsregler).
The four that catch people out in ordinary daily work:

- **No images of the screen:** the ban covers photos and screenshots alike, so
  you cannot snap a console output to paste into a message to a colleague.
- **Nothing leaves except through repatriation:** not by email, not on paper,
  not by retyping it. See [Phase 14 - Export and repatriation](export.qmd).
- **Never put real data in a written question:** when you describe a dataset or
  a problem to a colleague, a data manager or DST, use made-up examples. A
  pasted error message with a real `pnr` in it is a rule breach.
- **Work somewhere private:** your institution or your home workplace. Not a
  train, a bus, a café or a library. Log out of the server when you leave the
  screen, also for a short while; a screensaver is not enough. You may show
  your screen only to people who are approved for the data you are working
  with.

The full text is short and worth reading once: [Rules for working with microdata
(page in
Danish)](https://www.dst.dk/da/TilSalg/data-til-forskning/regler-og-datasikkerhed/regler-for-arbejdet-med-mikrodata).

## Log off correctly when you are done

Closing the remote window with the cross only disconnects you. DST's connection
guide says so directly: the programs you had open stay open on the server until
the next time you log on. A session left like that keeps holding the server's
RAM (see [Mind the RAM](good-coding-practice.qmd#mind-your-ram)).

Log off in this order:

1. **Log off the Python/R desktop** (where RStudio runs): use the Logoff icon on
   the desktop, or Sign out in the Start menu.
2. **Log off the FSE Windows desktop** in the same way, if you came in through
   it. Skip this step if you went straight to the Python/R desktop.
3. **Log out of [remote.dst.dk](https://remote.dst.dk) in your browser** with
   the Logout button at the top of the page.
